solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not an original way to increase the population

definitions.meaning: a copy made of a painting or antique rather than the genuine first piece
the breeding by which living things produce offspring

explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a reproduction, and breeding is reproduction, two separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Aspect is fancifully constructed — by me?

definitions.text: Aspect is fancifully constructed — by me?

indicators.note: putting the letters together in a fanciful new way signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a fanciful aspect of things is their own creation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a daydreamer is the very person who fancifully builds up an aspect of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer who retreats into fantasy constructs imaginary worlds, so the whole clue describes such a person.

clue.text: Stone found in grub — yuck!

indicators.note: the letters are found sitting inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a gem while grubbing about in something disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A red gemstone, so a precious stone.

clue.text: Care centre with no overnight charges

definitions.text: Care centre with no overnight charges

parts.words: Care centre with no overnight charges
parts.note: charges here are the children in someone's care, not fees, and they go home every night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' reads as money, but it means the children looked after; none stay overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where young children are minded during the working day, going home each evening.

clue.text: Observe upset in Argentinian fighter — must be something eaten

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the fighter's name

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to observe is to see

explanation.surface: A soldier from Argentina is warned that something must be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down, so the observed word is read bottom to top before going in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy food made from curdled milk, one example of something eaten.

clue.text: Disrepute of one fella naughtily grabbing maiden

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the shuffled letters grab hold of the maiden, enclosing her
behaving naughtily suggests the letters of the word are disordered

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A man disgraces himself by behaving badly with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' turns FELLA into LLFAE, which 'grabbing' wraps round M to give LLFAME after I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad reputation, as in a house of ill repute, is disrepute.

clue.text: Native showing fresh enthusiasm — a misguided nerd

parts.note: fresh means new
zeal is eager enthusiasm

indicators.note: a misguided word has gone astray, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A local shows newfound eagerness, according to a nerd who has got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' rearranges NERD to NDER, which ends the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in a Pacific nation, so a native of that country; the definition leaves the country to the wordplay.

clue.text: Very much hiding anger to appear as more reasonable

indicators.note: the first word hides the second inside it

parts.note: far means very much, as in far better
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone suppresses their fury so as to seem more reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning just or reasonable, so more reasonable.

clue.text: Brandy butter sent back — cold!

indicators.note: sending the word back means reading it in reverse

parts.note: a ram is a butter, an animal that butts
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: Brandy butter returned to the kitchen because it was served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brandy butter' looks like the Christmas sauce, but 'butter' is a ram, one that butts; 'sent back' turns RAM into MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A French brandy distilled from grape skins left after pressing.

clue.text: Heat up salad — it sounds like a bit of scientific theory

indicators.note: says the pieces are heard as the answer's sound

parts.note: to boil is to heat up, and slaw is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A cook warms up a salad, which turns out to sound like physics.
explanation.walkthrough: BOIL plus SLAW, spoken, gives the name of the gas law.
explanation.definitionFit: A law of physics relating pressure and volume of a gas, a piece of scientific theory.

clue.text: Producing some support and not being walked over

definitions.meaning: constructing a stand, a frame or rest that holds something up
refusing to be pushed around, holding firm against opposition

explanation.definitionFit: Literally constructing a support; idiomatically, resisting firmly instead of giving in.

clue.text: Short British game suitable for outside

indicators.note: the suitable word goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: apt means suitable
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A brief British sport that is best played outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Short in manner, curt, as in a brusque reply.

clue.text: Herb makes endless money by the way

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, such as prize money
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A herb earns its grower endless money on the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent plant used as a salad herb and pot herb.

clue.text: Writer Dickens has line about a saint, recluse

definitions.note: used as an adjective here, meaning living apart from the world

indicators.note: the writer's name goes about the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: Monica Dickens, the English novelist and great-granddaughter of Charles

explanation.surface: A novelist's book has a line about a holy hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer Dickens' tempts towards Charles, but the novelist meant is his great-granddaughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Of monks and their cloistered life, so withdrawn from the world like a hermit.

clue.text: Pensioners getting agitated, making reply

indicators.note: agitation stirs the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Retired people become stirred up as they answer back.
explanation.definitionFit: Said or done as an answer, so by way of a reply.

clue.text: Cruel hill

definitions.meaning: a moorland hill in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning savage, and a northern English word for a mountain or moor.

clue.text: Success the woman's got over time? Nothing, up to now

parts.note: a hit is a success
her stands for the woman
O, the shape of zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman's success came late, answered with: nothing so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Until this point, so up to now.

clue.text: Present soldier with source of financial information

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A soldier is given a business newspaper as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given freely, a gift.

clue.text: Terrible ruffian — such may get people taken for a ride

definitions.text: such may get people taken for a ride

indicators.note: something terrible is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful thug cheats people, taking them for a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for a ride' suggests a con; at a fairground it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fair with rides, where people are literally taken on rides.

clue.text: Like Ronald and Fiona having an affair!

definitions.text: Like Ronald and Fiona having an affair!

parts.words: Like Ronald and Fiona having an affair!
parts.note: a pair having an affair are behaving this way; the names are just any couple

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for conducting an illicit affair; the couple are invented.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for conducting a secret love affair.

clue.text: Good ground containing a source of energy

indicators.note: the first pieces contain the next one

parts.note: soil is ground or earth

explanation.surface: Fertile ground holds a source of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts A after the G, making G-A-SOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuel oil distilled from petroleum, used for heating and engines, so an energy source.

clue.text: Pair coming in celebrated and leapt in the air

indicators.note: the pair comes in, entering the other word

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it

explanation.surface: A couple arrive at the party, celebrate and jump for joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to jump, so leapt.

clue.text: Son along with daughter into messy paints — suitable things for kids playing

indicators.note: the daughter goes into the other letters
a messy word has its letters scattered out of order

explanation.surface: A boy and girl get into messy paints, ideal for children at play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' turns PAINTS into ANPITS, and 'into' puts D after ANPITS's first two letters, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxes of sand in which small children dig and play.

clue.text: Pursued, we hear, but morally pure

indicators.note: signals the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: chased means pursued

explanation.surface: Someone is chased by admirers yet stays virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from sex, so morally pure.

clue.text: Criminal offers opinion about ending in prison

indicators.note: the opinion goes about the next letter

parts.note: a bet is an opinion, as in my bet is

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A crook gives his view on finishing a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for corrupt or dishonest, so criminal.

clue.text: A new church established in a valley in the fall

indicators.note: set up inside, so these pieces go inside the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley

explanation.surface: A new chapel is built in a valley one autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the fall' reads as autumn, but the definition is a fall of snow; A-N-CH goes inside VALE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A great fall of snow and rock sliding down a mountainside.

clue.text: Scared when a female is taken in surprise attack

indicators.note: the letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: afraid means scared
A as written, and F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman is frightened when seized in a sudden assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden attack on an enemy or premises.

clue.text: Restrictions being removed? Lie around and get sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters reel about out of order

explanation.surface: Freed from rules, someone lounges about and gets drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The lifting of rules and controls, so restrictions being taken away.
